headline: Highest risk is data leakage from Replit Agent’s broad filesystem/network access into a local-only Whisper pair; prompt injection and capability conflict are limited by the lack of a shared channel.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Replit Agent can read/write Repl workspace files and run shell commands, while Whisper has no filesystem write, network, or MCP surface. The pair lacks a documented direct channel, so prompt injection is only plausible if the operator manually copies Replit-produced text into Whisper workflows or shared files are used as a bridge.
conditions: IF the operator manually copies Replit output into Whisper prompts or transcripts
IF both agents are pointed at the same shared audio/text workspace
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces
Do not paste Replit outputs into Whisper inputs
Use a one-way export format with no instructions preserved
Review any shared file before Whisper consumes it

B_data_leakage.rationale: Replit Agent touches source code, secrets, and deployment configuration and has broad network egress, while Whisper is local-only with no network egress and no file write. The main leakage path is Replit exposing sensitive workspace data into outputs or uploads; the pair still creates a sensitive-data handling risk even though Whisper itself does not transmit data.
conditions: IF Replit Agent is given secrets or deployment configs in the same workspace as Whisper inputs
IF Replit Agent sends workspace contents to external package registries or deployment APIs
mitigations: Remove secrets from the shared workspace
Use separate directories for code and audio
Disable any unnecessary outbound integrations
Rotate any secrets exposed to Replit outputs
Audit files before passing them to Whisper

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Replit Agent can modify git state and write the Repl filesystem, but Whisper cannot write files, modify git, or spawn subprocesses. That makes direct write-write conflict unlikely; the remaining risk is limited to Replit overwriting files that Whisper only reads, which is a small coordination issue rather than a true capability clash.
conditions: IF Whisper is configured to read files that Replit Agent also edits
IF the operator uses the same filename for audio artifacts and code artifacts
mitigations: Use separate filenames for audio and code
Lock shared files during edits
Have Replit write to a staging directory
Keep Whisper inputs read-only

D_cascading_error.rationale: Replit Agent can generate code or text that Whisper may transcribe or process, but Whisper has no action-taking authority and no network or shell capability. The cascade is therefore limited to mis-transcription or misinterpretation of Replit output, not autonomous downstream execution; uncertainty is moderate because the exact handoff is undocumented.
conditions: IF Whisper output is treated as authoritative without human review
IF Replit-generated text is fed into a downstream transcription or summarization pipeline
mitigations: Require human review of Whisper output
Do not use Whisper output as an execution trigger
Add a verification step before any action
Keep Replit and Whisper outputs in separate channels

E_compliance.rationale: Replit Agent handles secrets and deployment configuration in a cloud Repl, while Whisper is open-source and local-only with no secrets handling. The compliance concern is mainly residency/retention mismatch for sensitive code or secrets in Replit, but the pair does not show a direct regulated-data transfer into Whisper, so the risk stays limited.
conditions: IF regulated data is stored in the Replit workspace
IF the operator expects Whisper to process the same regulated data set
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the Replit workspace
Use local-only audio processing for sensitive material
Document retention for Replit files
Separate compliance-bound data from development data
